# Infinite Fourier hierarchy generated by hidden drive phase

**Date:** 2026-11-11  
**Author:** Felipe Gianini Romero  
**Status:** exact analytic consequence of the randomized-phase protocol  
**Novelty status:** Fourier/Bessel expansions and hidden-variable hierarchies are classical; project-specific physical interpretation only

## 1. Question

The phase-averaged transform equation contains

$$
\operatorname{Cov}_\phi
(\Gamma_\phi^+,G_{c,\phi}).
$$

It would be misleading to treat that covariance as one additional state variable that automatically closes the problem.

The exact conditioned dynamics show that marginalizing the phase creates an infinite Fourier hierarchy for nonzero drive amplitude.

## 2. Lift the hidden phase back into the state

For a fixed repetition, the phase \(\phi\) is constant while the current drive angle is

$$
\theta=\omega t+\phi.
$$

Let

$$
U(t,\theta)
$$

denote the conditioned transform \(G_{c,\phi}(t)\) expressed in the current phase coordinate.

The exact conditioned scalar equation becomes

$$
\boxed{
\partial_t U
+
\omega\partial_\theta U
=
-\kappa\Gamma_0
e^{-A\sin\theta}U
+
b,
}
$$

where

$$
\kappa=1-e^{-c},
\qquad
A=\beta eS_{\rm AC},
\qquad
b=D(e^c-1).
$$

The phase-averaged transform is the zeroth Fourier mode of \(U\).

## 3. Fourier expansion of the drive

Write

$$
U(t,\theta)
=
\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}
u_n(t)e^{in\theta}.
$$

The modified-Bessel generating function gives

$$
e^{-A\sin\theta}
=
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}
\gamma_m(A)e^{im\theta},
$$

with coefficients equal to modified Bessel functions up to phase factors.

A convenient complex convention is

$$
\gamma_m(A)=i^m I_m(A),
$$

because

$$
-\sin\theta=\cos(\theta+\pi/2).
$$

For \(A>0\),

$$
I_m(A)>0
$$

for every nonnegative integer \(m\).

Thus the drive has infinitely many nonzero Fourier harmonics whenever the drive amplitude is nonzero.

## 4. Exact Fourier hierarchy

Substituting the Fourier series into the lifted PDE gives

$$
\boxed{
\dot u_n
=
-in\omega u_n
-
\kappa\Gamma_0
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}
\gamma_m(A)u_{n-m}
+
b\,\delta_{n0}.
}
$$

The phase average is

$$
\bar G_c=u_0.
$$

Its exact derivative is

$$
\boxed{
\dot u_0
=
-\kappa\Gamma_0
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}
\gamma_m(A)u_{-m}
+
b.
}
$$

Therefore the zeroth mode is coupled to the full Fourier tower.

## 5. Infinite modes are generated immediately

Suppose the initial distribution is independent of the randomized phase.

Then

$$
U(0,\theta)=G_0
$$

is constant, so

$$
u_0(0)=G_0,
\qquad
u_n(0)=0
\quad(n\neq0).
$$

For \(n\neq0\),

$$
\boxed{
\dot u_n(0)
=
-\kappa\Gamma_0
\gamma_n(A)G_0.
}
$$

For nonzero drive amplitude \(A>0\),

$$
\gamma_n(A)\neq0
$$

for every integer harmonic.

Hence infinitely many phase modes are generated at the first derivative even if the initial state contains only the average mode.

This gives an exact strengthening of the covariance obstruction:

$$
\boxed{
\text{phase marginalization creates an infinite exact hierarchy.}
}
$$

## 6. Relation to the paper's Fourier treatment

The experimental paper uses Fourier expansion of the periodically driven master equation and truncates the harmonic representation numerically.

That is fully consistent with the structure above.

A finite harmonic cutoff is a computational approximation to an exact hierarchy with infinite Fourier support when \(A\neq0\).

The present note does not claim a new Fourier method.

Its role is to identify precisely what information is lost when the phase is removed from the physical-bridge state.

## 7. Why one covariance is not enough

The zeroth-mode equation can be written using one covariance,

$$
\dot{\bar G}_c
=
-\kappa\bar\Gamma\,\bar G_c+b
-\kappa\operatorname{Cov}_\phi(\Gamma_\phi^+,G_{c,\phi}).
$$

But the time evolution of that covariance depends on higher mixed phase moments.

The Fourier representation makes this nonclosure explicit and systematic: the hidden information is not generically one scalar correction but an infinite sequence of phase modes.

## 8. Continuous versus stroboscopic information

This result should be read together with the Floquet note.

At arbitrary continuous time:

$$
u_0
\longleftrightarrow
u_{\pm1},u_{\pm2},\ldots
$$

through an infinite hierarchy.

At integer drive periods, however, the phase-conditioned monodromy has phase-independent diagonal Floquet multipliers. Cayley-Hamilton then produces exact finite recurrences for phase-averaged commensurate transforms.

Thus:

$$
\boxed{
\text{continuous-time exact description can require infinite hidden-phase information}
}
$$

while

$$
\boxed{
\text{stroboscopic sampling can restore finite exact closure}.
}
$$

The information required by a coarse description therefore depends not only on the observable and dynamics but also on the temporal resolution at which the system is represented.

## 9. Scientific boundary

This note does not introduce a new physical field, hidden degree of freedom, or entropy variable.

The phase is already part of the experimental control protocol.

The result says only that discarding a real control coordinate can make an otherwise closed conditioned observable nonclosed, and that the exact marginal description carries the lost dependence through an infinite Fourier hierarchy.

No spacetime or pregeometric interpretation follows.
